fatal_errors: The proposed experiment does not test reduced platinum-group-metal consumption: the candidate contains approximately 1 wt% Pd, while the control loading is unspecified, and no equal-performance lower-loading comparison is included.
Changing both Pd dispersion and support composition prevents attribution of any improvement specifically to isolated Pd atoms.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible alternative rather than a reconstruction of the target. It addresses exhaust-catalyst activity and durability through single-atom Pd on a high-entropy oxide, whereas the target concerns closed-loop high-throughput optimization of multielement alloys on La-doped gamma-Al2O3, severe cyclic ageing, and ageing-induced Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction. E3 directly supports the proposed vacancy-enhanced Pd single-atom mechanism and stability; E1 only indirectly supports configurational-disorder benefits, and E2 is largely generic. The experiment has quantitative light-off and durability criteria and suitable structural measurements, but it omits the target's severe 900 °C ageing, near-stoichiometric multicomponent feed, species-resolved NO and hydrocarbon conversion, and statistical discovery comparison. Most importantly, its design cannot establish the claimed reduction in PGM use because catalyst loadings are not explicitly varied or matched on performance.
